title: Detection of membrane-anchoring lipid modifications of proteins in cells by radioactive metabolic labeling
protocol: Split cells a day before transfection into 6 cm dishes so that they reach 70% confluency on the transfection day.
Incubate cells in 4 mL DMEM containing 5% dialyzed serum and 15 μM lovastatin for 2 hours for prenylation assays.
Thaw plasmids and PEI Max at room temperature.
Add optiMEM (100 μL/μg DNA) into 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes.
Add plasmids (1–5 μg/6 cm culture dish) to the optiMEM containing tubes.
Add PEI Max at a ratio of 3:1 (ratio of PEI to DNA) and mix by flicking or alternatively brief careful vortexing.
Incubate the tubes at room temperature for 10–15 min.
Add 2 mL of fresh DMEM containing 5% dialyzed serum, 400 μCi of concentrated H3-mevalonolactone (0.2 mCi/mL) and 15 μM lovastatin to the 6 cm dishes for prenylation labeling.
Change the medium of the 6 cm dishes to 2 mL of labeling medium containing 0.2 mCi/mL of concentrated H3-palmitic acid for palmitoylation labeling.
Add the transfection mixture dropwise to cells.
Mix well by back-and-forth dish shaking.
Incubate the cells overnight at 37°C in the CO2 incubator.
Remove the medium from the plates.
Add 1 mL PBS to the plates and scrape the cells.
Pipette up and down and transfer the cells into a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Wash the plate once with 1 mL PBS to recover residual cells.
Combine the 1 mL wash with scraped cells in the same 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C to pellet down the cells.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL PBS.
Transfer the mixture into a fresh 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 4°C and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μL lysis buffer containing 1× PIC.
Incubate on ice for 30 min with intermittent vortexing.
Sonicate the lysate for 3 min (pulse on: 10 s, pulse off: 10 s, and Amplitude: 30%) in Sonic Dismembrator with Cup Horn.
Dispose of all liquid washes according to the liquid radioactivity disposal guidelines.
Use Cup Horn for sonication in cold distilled water to avoid contamination and sample degradation.
Centrifuge tubes at 21000 × g for 20 min.
Transfer supernatants to separate 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Aliquot 10% of the samples as input in a separate 1.5 mL tube.
Add 4× sample buffer containing freshly added DTT (50 mM) to a final concentration of 1×.
Heat at 70°C for 10 min.
Cool at room temperature.
Give a short spin (full speed) in a tabletop centrifuge.
Store samples at -20°C.
Wash rProtein G Agarose and M2-FLAG-Agarose Gel in lysis buffer without PIC 2–3 times, each time centrifuging at 350 × g for 3 min and aspirating the supernatant.
Resuspend the pelleted beads in lysis buffer as a 50% mixture (1:1 mixing).
Centrifuge M2-FLAG-Agarose Gel at 5000 g for 30 s if needed.
Aliquot 40 μL of the washed rProtein G Agarose into fresh 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Cut the front portion of a 200 μL pipette tip with clean scissors to make a wider bore for homogenous aliquoting.
Add labeled protein samples to microcentrifuge tubes containing aliquoted rProtein G Agarose and mix by flicking gently to preclear the samples.
Rotate the samples for 1–2 hours at 4°C (∼16 rpm).
Spin the samples at 350 × g for 3 minutes and add supernatants into microcentrifuge tubes containing aliquoted M2-FLAG-Agarose Gel.
Mix by flicking gently.
Rotate samples for 1–16 hours at 4°C (∼16 rpm).
Rotate samples between 1-16 hours based on the expression levels of the target protein.
Optimize IP duration for endogenous proteins without radiolabeling beforehand if necessary.
Add 30–50 μL of washed rProtein A/G Agarose resin (50% mixture) and incubate for 1-2 hours if antibody is not conjugated to resin.
Spin the samples and wash 3 times with lysis buffer without PIC, centrifuging at 350 × g for 3 min each time.
Remove supernatant from washed samples.
Add 20–30 μL of 2× sample buffer to samples and denature at 98°C for 10 minutes.
Cool the tubes at room temperature and spin briefly at full speed.
Store samples at -20°C or -80°C before loading.
Elute with 3X-FLAG peptide in TBS (concentration and volumes optimized) as an alternative to direct buffer reconstitution.
Run samples on BoltTM 4%–12% Bis-Tris Plus gel at 150 V for 50 minutes.
Activate the PVDF membrane by wetting it in methanol for a few seconds and equilibrating in transfer buffer until it sinks.
Transfer the samples at 20 V for 1 h in an InvitrogenTM Mini Gel Tank.
Stain the PVDF membrane with Ponceau S to confirm the proper transfer of proteins.
Wash the membrane with TBST (0.1% Tween-20).
Stain with Ponceau S until color develops.
Wash with distilled water to remove the background.
De-stain with TBST.
Wash with PBS/TBS once before next step.
Air dry the PVDF membrane on filter paper, carefully monitoring the orientation of top vs. bottom sides.
Expose PVDF membrane to phosphor screen and detect using a phosphor imager.
Cover the PVDF membrane with a phosphor screen in a cassette.
Use low adhesion tape to secure the phosphor screen.
Close the cassette tightly.
Place the cassette at room temperature in darkness for 2–3 weeks exposure.
Remove the phosphor screen from the cassette after exposure.
Detect the H3 signal using a phosphor imager.
Take a colorimetric image of the PVDF membrane if using a colorimetric molecular weight marker.
Process the PVDF membrane for Western blotting.
Block the PVDF membrane in 5% nonfat dry milk.
Immunoblot for the transfected target protein with rabbit anti-FLAG antibody.
